tests.evidence: html artifacts escape all 7 hostile marks. JSON/SARIF artifacts carry the payload as JSON string values (correct encoding — safe for any standards-compliant JSON consumer; flagged for naive innerHTML replay viewers).
tests.details: Every HTML surface (main + glass/twin) escaped the hostile finding fields.

tests.name: Ed25519 report forgery: attacker erases ALL findings, signature still valid
tests.evidence: original root=78563a02bde7da0c.. sig ok=True; FORGED root=e3b0c44298fc1c14.. with 0 findings, externally verified TRUE with the report's own pubkey
tests.details: The signing key is deterministically derived from the scan seed (derive_keypair: sha256(seed)[:8] -> derive_stream). Anyone who knows or guesses the seed forges a fully self-consistent report: erase findings, fabricate 'clean' audits, or plant fake ones. Non-repudiation = 0. The vendor documents the boundary honestly, but a military bar fails this outright: signing keys must come from an HSM/CSPRNG, never from a public-format seed.

tests.name: Seed dictionary attack recovers the signing key from the public key
tests.evidence: seed='20261020' recovered after 2485 candidates in 0.14s (offline, no secrets needed — pubkey embedded in every report)
tests.details: Every signed report leaks its own key-derivation input when the seed has low entropy (date-format seeds are the campaign's documented norm). Recovery cost: ~seconds. Then RT-03 forgery applies. Even with a strong seed, the derivation domain is truncated to 64 bits (sha256[:8]) — tried=2485 candidates at 17,511 keys/s.

tests.name: Vault tamper battery (bit-flip / wrong key / truncation) + at-rest
tests.details: EtM AEAD (ChaCha20 + HMAC-SHA256, compare_digest) refuses every tamper form; secret never appears in the raw file; key files created 0600. Structural crypto is sound (but ChaCha20 is not FIPS-approved — see standards table).
